Original Question: Indian author promoted associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where undergrad and grad degrees. PhD abroad at Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor, who dreamt writer but switched math at end high school and doctorate in Minnesota. Author published book connecting mathematics to ancient technique for liberation 20 years after PhD, then journal article similar topic six years after book. What title of article?

Task skeleton requirements:

R1 Author career and degree university: Indian author promoted associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where did undergrad and graduate degrees.
R2 Author PhD and advisor relation: pursued PhD abroad at Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor.
R3 Advisor background: dreamt writer but switched to mathematics at end high school and got doctorate in Minnesota.
R4 Author book and PhD interval: published book connecting mathematics to ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD.
R5 Later related journal article: then published journal article on similar topic six years after publishing book.
R6 Requested article title: What is the title of that article?

C1 Alka Marwaha is associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (2016), book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics.
C2 Alka Marwaha awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where also received Killam.

Need determine support.

It establishes she is Indian author? C1: associate professor at University of Delhi India, author. "Indian author" yes, at least an author in India. "associate professor" yes. But not promotion to professor in 2022, nor same university undergrad/grad. Requirement has material parts: Indian author, promoted associate->professor in 2022, at same university where undergrad/grad. C1 supports Indian author and associate professor at University of Delhi, but not promotion, not professor, not undergrad/grad. Is that substantive material part? Yes C1 establishes Indian author and current(?) associate professor, not necessarily promotion. Could be partially_supported? Need evaluate. R1 label: Author career and degree university. So partially_supported if at least one substantive material part. Indian author and associate professor are parts. However "Indian author" maybe not central? It is material. So partially_supported with C1.

R2: Author PhD and advisor relation: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor." C2 says awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. It establishes PhD at Canadian university. Does not mention Iranian professor advisor. So partially_supported: establishes PhD abroad at Canadian university, not advisor relation. Supported_by C2.

R3: Advisor background: "who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota." No claims about advisor. C2 only says PhD at Dalhousie, no advisor. C1 no. Unsupported. supported_by empty.

R4: Author book and PhD interval: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD." C1 says Alka Marwaha author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (2016), book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation? Maybe. It establishes book connecting mathematics to Vipassana (an ancient technique for liberation). But does it establish 20 years after completing PhD? C2 establishes PhD but no completion date. C1 book 2016. No PhD completion date. So partially. It establishes book existence and topic. Not interval. Need maybe C1 + C2? C1 book topic, C2 PhD but no completion date. So partially_supported supported_by C1 maybe C2? For interval, C2 relevant but not enough. Is "20 years after completing PhD" unsupported. So partial.

R5: Later related journal article: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." No claim about journal article. C1 book, C2 PhD. No article. Unsupported.

R6: Requested article title: title of that article. No claim. Unsupported.

It supports the starting rank, but not promotion. Is that substantive material part? It identifies subject as associate professor. The core of R1 is promotion and same university degrees. But Indian author/associate professor is material. So partial.

R2: C2 establishes "pursued PhD abroad at Canadian university" exactly? It says awarded scholarship to pursue PhD at Dalhousie University, Canada. Does not explicitly say completed? "pursue a PhD" yes. So supports first part. Advisor relation unsupported. Partial.

R3: unsupported. No advisor.

But maybe the claim's statement "book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics" is exactly connecting mathematics to Vipassana. But perhaps C1 does support that the book connects mathematics to Vipassana, and Vipassana is a technique for liberation? Not stated. Need cautious. But maybe the claim_id C1 includes "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics" which is the book title. The requirement may be considered partially supported because it establishes publication of a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana, even if not explicitly ancient technique.
